events.title: A solar eclipse marks Mursili II's campaign against Hayasa-Azzi
events.description: In the tenth year of the Hittite king Mursili II, as he was about to launch a campaign against the Kingdom of Hayasa-Azzi, "the Sun gave a sign": an eclipse that most scholars date to this day. It is of great importance for dating the Hittite Empire.

events.title: Western Roman emperor Glycerius is forced to abdicate
events.description: Glycerius, proclaimed emperor of the West in March 473 by the magister militum Gundobad and not recognised by the Eastern emperor Leo I, was forced to abdicate. The Western Roman Empire ended in 476, when the last emperor was deposed.

events.title: Mieszko I of Poland defeats Margrave Hodo near the Oder
events.description: An army led by Mieszko I of Poland defeated the forces of the Saxon margrave Hodo near the Oder river, the first documented victory of Polish forces. Whether the battle took place near the modern town of Cedynia is disputed.

events.title: Afonso Henriques defeats his mother's forces at São Mamede
events.description: Near Guimarães, Afonso Henriques defeated the forces of his mother, Countess Teresa, and her Galician ally Fernão Peres de Trava. The victory gave him control of the County of Portugal and is traditionally seen as the founding event of Portuguese independence.

events.title: Robert the Bruce routs Edward II at Bannockburn
events.description: On the second day, Scottish spearmen drove the English army into the burns and marshes near Stirling. Edward II fled, and Scotland's independence was secured until England recognised it in 1328.
events.html: On the second day, Scottish spearmen drove the English army into the burns and marshes near Stirling. Edward II fled, and Scotland's independence was secured until England recognised it in 1328.

events.title: Edward III destroys the French fleet at Sluys
events.description: The English fleet of King Edward III attacked the French fleet assembled for an invasion of England in the Zwin estuary off Sluis, in Flanders, and destroyed it almost entirely. The victory gave England control of the Channel for years.

events.title: An outbreak of dancing mania begins in Aachen
events.description: One of the biggest outbreaks of dancing mania, in which groups of people danced erratically, allegedly until they collapsed from exhaustion, began in Aachen. It spread to Cologne, Flanders, Metz, Strasbourg, Utrecht and other places, and to Italy.

events.title: John Cabot makes landfall in North America
events.description: Sailing for Henry VII, the Venetian navigator John Cabot landed on the coast, probably of Newfoundland or Cape Breton. His voyage became the basis of later English claims in North America.

events.title: Premier Grand Lodge of England is founded
events.description: Four London lodges met at the Goose and Gridiron alehouse to form a Grand Lodge. It marks the beginning of organised modern Freemasonry.
events.html: Four London lodges met at the Goose and Gridiron alehouse to form a Grand Lodge. It marks the beginning of organised modern Freemasonry.

events.title: Napoleon's Grande Armée crosses the Niemen into Russia
events.description: Some 450,000 troops in the first wave crossed into Russian territory. By December only a fraction had survived the retreat from Moscow.
events.html: Some 450,000 troops in the first wave crossed into Russian territory. By December only a fraction had survived the retreat from Moscow.

events.title: Soviet Union begins the Berlin Blockade
events.description: Soviet forces cut road, rail and canal links to West Berlin. The Western Allies responded with an airlift that supplied the city's two million people for eleven months.

song: A Russian love song from 1843, sung to a waltz tune of 1879. It became one of the best-known Russian songs abroad.
